tagline: Named for a governor, not the parks, but it finds them.
intro: The byway picks up the Parks Highway at the edge of Denali State Park and runs north beside the Alaska Railroad. It crosses Hurricane Gulch, tops Broad Pass at 2,400 feet, comes down past Cantwell and the road into Denali National Park, and ends at Healy, where coal mining began in 1918.

The name fools people. The road was finished in 1971 as the Anchorage-Fairbanks Highway and renamed for George A. Parks, territorial governor from 1925 to 1933, though the aptness was noticed at the time. Its mileposts count from downtown Anchorage, which the highway never enters.

moments.title: Byers Lake
moments.text: A small lake named for a fisherman the bush pilot Don Sheldon flew in many times in the 1950s, with the Alaska Veterans Memorial on the hilltop beside it.

moments.title: Hurricane Gulch
moments.text: The highway has its own bridge here. Just downstream the railroad's 1921 steel arch stands 296 feet over the creek, for eight years the tallest bridge in the country.

moments.title: Broad Pass
moments.text: A gap of about 15 miles in the Alaska Range, recorded by USGS geologists in 1898. The railroad came through in 1923 and the highway, in no hurry, in 1971.
